task.question: На каком прыжке упала Аделия Петросян в произвольной программе на зимних Олимпийских играх 2026 года?
task.evidence: Аделия Петросян (AIN) — 6 место, 214,53 (короткая 72,89 — 5; произвольная 141,64 — 5). Упала при исполнении четверного тулупа в произвольной программе.

На Олимпиаде 2026 года в произвольной программе Аделия Петросян упала на **четверном тулупе (quadruple toe loop)**. FINAL: четверной тулуп

She is a three-time Russian national champion (2024, 2025, 2026) and a three-time Russian Grand Prix Final champion (2023, 2024, 2025). Internationally, she is the 2021 JGP Slovenia champion and the 2025 Skate to Milano champion. She went undefeated in all domestic skating competitions during the 2023–2024 and the 2024–2025 seasons. She competed at the 2026 Winter Olympics as an Individual Neutral Athlete.

She competed at the 2026 Winter Olympics as an Individual Neutral Athlete.
During her free skate performance, Petrosian attempted a quadruple toe loop but the jump was deemed to be underrotated.
She became first woman to land a quadruple loop in competition; however, because the jump was landed in a domestic competition, it could not be recognized officially by the International Skating Union.
Going on to compete at the 2023 Russian Championships, Petrosian ranked in fifth place in the short program after falling on a planned triple Lutz.
She won the short program segment after landing all of her jumps cleanly, including a planned triple Axel.
The following month, she took the individual silver at the Russian Figure Skating Jumping Championships, behind Margarita Bazyliuk and ahead of Elena Kostyleva.
In May 2025, the International Skating Union (ISU) announced that Petrosian as well as Alina Gorbacheva had both been approved as Individual Neutral Athletes (AIN), making them both eligible to compete at the 2025 ISU Olympic Qualifying Competition to vie for a spot to compete at the 2026 Winter Olympics.
At the event, she opted to not attempt any quadruple jumps due to them being inconsistent following her injury's recovery.
In late November, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) officially declared Petrosian as eligible to compete at the 2026 Winter Olympics.
On 17 February, Petrosian competed in the short program at the 2026 Winter Olympics, where she delivered a clean skate and placed fifth in that segment.
She and her coaching team decided to include two quadruple jumps, recognising their importance for a chance at the podium.
Petrosian was the only competitor to attempt a quadruple toe-loop, but she fell on the jump.
This lead her to omit the second quadruple jump planned in her program, and she managed to skate the rest of the program cleanly.
